messages:
carmen: heads up — saw a handful of requests routed to v1 even though clients sent X-Redwood-Version: 2.0. Not consistent across regions.

drew: huh, do we have any recent routing rule changes? I thought affinity was based on the version header first, then token mapping.

anya: @drew I pushed a small tweak to the header-negotiation last week to prefer cookie-affinity for legacy clients. Could be the change.

carmen: here's an example request we logged:
```
POST /v2/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer tok_XXXX
X-Redwood-Version: 2
Cookie: rw_client_affinity=legacy-123
```
It ended up on a v1 pool.

drew: thanks — that cookie should only win if header missing. I'll pull tracing for the exact path. Infra bot, did the rollout flip set for header precedence? @infra-bot

infra-bot: deploy-ops: rollout flag "version.affinity.precedence" set to "cookie,header" in us-west-2 at 2938475100 by deploy-bot.

anya: oh shoot, that was me while testing an A/B for enterprise customers. I meant to scope it to a feature flag but accidentally toggled the global rollout. My bad.

carmen: ok that explains it. Two follow-ups: (1) we need a rollback/patch to restore header-first precedence, (2) console UX should show that flag prominently in the versioning dashboard and surface which customers are affected.

drew: +1 on both. For telemetry: we should emit a signal when actual routed_version != client_version header. That'll make it easy to alert.

anya: agree. Also suggest a rate/quota check: if we reroute v2 traffic to v1 pools they might hit v1 quotas unexpectedly. We should mark rerouted requests in quota accounting as the client-intended version.

carmen: good point — charging/counters need to reflect the header if present. Otherwise customers see weird billing deltas.

drew: implementation plan:
- infra: flip flag back to "header,cookie" (fast)
- runtime: add telemetry metric route_mismatch{region, routed, header} (short)
- quota: tag requests with intended_version header for accounting (medium)
- console: add a small banner on the Versioning page showing active precedence order and recent flips (UX)

anya: I'll flip the flag now and push a console mock for the banner. ping me for design review @anya.

infra-bot: deploy-ops: flag updated to "header,cookie" in us-west-2 at 2938475160 by anya. No downstream deploy required.

carmen: thanks. Drew, can you add a short alert rule that fires if route_mismatch rate > 0.1% for 10m? We want to catch any accidental global toggles quickly.

drew: on it. Also adding a low-severity billing dashboard that compares billed-by-routed vs billed-by-intended for last 24h so CS can triage.

anya: console banner mock: "Version precedence: header → cookie → token. Click to view recent changes." I'll link the changelog entry to the flag mutation log.

carmen: perfect. One last thing — let's make the console show an override control but require 2-step confirmation and admin role. We don't want accidental global flips.

drew: yep. Add an audit modal and require the reason field. We'll also enforce scoped rollouts by default.

carmen: thanks all. Followups: @anya create PR for banner + flag audit modal; @drew telemetry + alert; infra keep an eye on any other regions still on the old order.

console-bot: note: related doc created at internal.redwood/docs/versioning-precedence. Reference ID: INT-2026-41.

anya: PR opened: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4123 — includes banner screenshot and admin modal.

drew: tracing shows the behavior spike between 2938475105–2938475160, region eu-central unaffected.

carmen: closing loop — customer-impacting? Any errors or increased latency from reroutes?

drew: no latency spikes, just quota mismatches for a small set of enterprise integrations. CS notified.

carmen: okay great. I'll draft a short tech note for the status channel summarizing cause + mitigation.

anya: thanks — will follow up with a smaller scope feature-flag permission change to prevent global toggles.

carmen: done. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
